I'm Joon-i. Every night I fall asleep in my cape.
Because... I'm going to be a hero who saves the world, very soon!
Joon-i didn't forget his cape again today.
A cape is a must, even for school! Swoooosh!
The lunch bell rang,
and Joon-i dashed off, his cape flying behind him.
To protect the Earth, I need to store up lots of energy.
I'm first in line! Swoooosh!
Hey, we've all been waiting here...
Heroes are fast. That's just how it is!
Joon-i shoved the board game away and burst into tears.
Waaah! I can't lose! That's impossible!
Play again! This game doesn't count!
No one came near Joon-i.
He sat all alone on the empty playground swing,
listening to his friends laughing and playing far away.
Everyone's having fun... except me.
Just then, he heard someone crying on the other side of the swings.
Seon-ho had fallen on his crutches and scraped his knee.
Joon-i stretched out both arms and squeezed his eyes shut,
but nothing happened.
I'll save you!
Wound-healing laser beam, fire!!
Just then, Min-ji ran over and sat down beside Seon-ho.
She lowered herself down
and waited until Seon-ho was ready to stand.
Seon-ho held onto Min-ji's shoulder and finally got up.
Seon-ho, that must really hurt...
Take your time getting up. I've got you.
Thank you, Min-ji.
The teacher came over and praised Min-ji,
and the other kids clapped.
It was strange.
Min-ji had no laser,
no superpowers, and yet everybody liked her.
She hadn't saved the Earth. She didn't even have a cape.
She was just like... a hero.
Joon-i looked down at his droopy cape.
What do I... have to do
to become a hero people like?
From that day on, Joon-i carried a little notebook
and secretly watched Min-ji.
Min-ji, greeting everyone first on the way to school.
Min-ji, raising her hand and waiting her turn to speak.
Min-ji, smiling and clapping even for the losing team.
Joon-i drew each one in his notebook.
Joon-i, why do you keep staring at me?
N-no! It's nothing...
A few days later, there was a dodgeball game in gym class.
Joon-i's team lost.
Some of his friends grumbled, upset about it.
Joon-i hesitated for a moment.
In the past, he would have shouted, "No way!
Play again!"
Joon-i took a deep breath
and walked over to the winning team.
The classroom went quiet.
Everyone looked at Joon-i.
Min-ji too.
You guys were really good earlier... Congratulations!
It was lunchtime, and the line was long.
Joon-i started to dash to the front...
but stopped, and went to the back of the line.
When Seon-ho came slowly along on his crutches,
Joon-i stepped aside to make room for him.
Seon-ho, stand in front of me. Take your time.
Oh... thanks, Joon-i. Want to eat lunch together?
Huh? S-sure! Okay!
That night, Joon-i opened his notebook.
Inside, the hero badges he had drawn
were growing, one by one.
He took off his cape, laid it neatly beside the notebook,
and looked at the moon outside the window.
I think... I was a little bit of a hero today.
Will Joon-i wear his cape tomorrow?
Probably.
But now he knows.
True power isn't in a cape,
it's the heart inside.
